diagnostics.message: `:resource.local_file.public_ssh_key` has an explicit `depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"]` that duplicates the dependency already established by `content = "${tls_private_key.ssh.public_key_openssh}"` (the graph already records `:resource.tls_private_key.ssh` in implicit_deps). The `depends_on` can be dropped.

`:resource.local_file.private_ssh_key` has an explicit `depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"]` that duplicates the dependency already established by `content = "${tls_private_key.ssh.private_key_pem}"` (the graph already records `:resource.tls_private_key.ssh` in implicit_deps). The `depends_on` can be dropped.

`module.runner:resource.aws_launch_configuration.gitlab_runner_instance` launches instances whose user-data registers the runner and writes the registration token into the SSM parameter named by `local.secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key`, but it has no dependency on `module.runner:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token` (that node has zero edges in the graph). The parameter is created by Terraform with `value = "null"` and `lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["value"] }`. If the ASG's instances start before the parameter exists, user-data creates it and stores the real token; Terraform then creates its own parameter with value `null` afterwards and, because `value` is ignored on subsequent applies, the token is permanently lost and the runner never registers. The launch configuration (and therefore the ASG) must be ordered after the SSM parameter.
